title: You think you’re too dirty for God?
paragraphs: You think you’re too dirty for God?
Then why did Jesus walk straight into the mess?

Because the part of your story you’re hiding…
is the exact place God is reaching.

Not after you fix it.
Not after you clean it up.

You smile in public.
You serve.
You show up.

Like if people really knew…
if they saw the thoughts, the habits, the relapse, the secret sin…

You perform.
You pretend.
You push.
Because shame doesn’t leave through effort.

It hides.
It buries.
It whispers.
Some of you aren’t running from sin anymore.

You’re running from God
because of your sin.

That quiet distance.
That hesitation to pray.
That guilt when you hear His name.
That’s shame wearing a religious mask.

Romans 5:8
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not after.
Not once you improved.
Not when you became “church-ready.”
While you were still in it.

Still addicted.
Still compromised.
Still confused.
Still failing.

Some scholars emphasize that Paul uses this verse to show the timing of God’s love—
that it is not a response to human righteousness,
but the very source of it.
God didn’t love you because you changed.
You change because He loved you.

Because religion says:
“Fix yourself, then come.”

Jesus says:
“Come, and I will fix what you cannot.”

Not as decoration.
Not as symbol.

2 Corinthians 5:21
“God made Him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”
Do you understand what that means?
Jesus didn’t just carry your mistakes.
And it was nailed to wood.

So when you say,
“I’m too far gone…”

You’re actually saying:
“The cross wasn’t enough.”
God is not shocked by what you did.

He saw it
before the cross.

It separates.
It destroys.
It hardens the heart.

Romans 6:23
“For the wages of sin is death…”
“…but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.”

Jesus didn’t die
so you can stay the same.

He died
to make you new.

Luke 5:32
“I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

God loves you
in your unworthiness.

But He loves you too much
to leave you there.
The prodigal son didn’t stay in the pigpen.

Luke 15:20
“But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion for him; he ran to his son…”
God is not waiting with crossed arms.

So what are you doing
still rehearsing your guilt?

Still punishing yourself
for what Jesus already paid?

1 John 1:9
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.”
Because grace was never for the worthy.
But don’t stay as you are.

Jesus is ready to forgive,
restore,
and rebuild your life
from the inside out.
